items.title: UK GDPR, Article 35: Data protection impact assessment
items.why: The assessment must be done 'prior to the processing' where high risk to people is likely. The one pre-deployment gate that UK law imposes. No outstanding changes shown on the day checked.

items.title: UK GDPR, Article 36: Prior consultation
items.why: Source of the figure: written advice within up to eight weeks, extendable by six. The text now reads 'the Commission', substituted on 30 September 2026 by S.I. 2026/386 (note F2).

items.title: Data protection impact assessments: Do we need to consult the ICO?
items.locator: Sections 'When do we need to consult the ICO?', 'How long does it take?' and 'What are the possible outcomes?'
items.why: Source of the quotation. Also states the regulator may impose a limitation or ban on intended processing, and a maximum of 14 weeks. Under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act; page carries no date, year is the year read.

items.title: UK GDPR, Article 83: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
items.why: Fines up to £8,700,000 or 2% of worldwide annual turnover for breach of controller obligations in Articles 25 to 39, which include Articles 35 and 36.

items.title: Data and AI Ethics Framework
items.publisher: Government Digital Service / Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.locator: Accountability principle; passage on human oversight ('the right choice might be to not use the system at all')
items.why: Guidance for public bodies, not law. Defines accountability as governance, oversight and routes to challenge. It does not prescribe an ethics board or a stop/go authority.

items.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
items.locator: Policy Area 1: Ethical impact assessment, paras 50-53
items.why: Para 50 asks Member States to introduce frameworks for impact assessments, such as ethical impact assessment. Addressed to states; not binding on companies.
